title: Float keys beyond the range of a double are different keys when their values differ
notes: `1e400` and `2e400` stand for 10^400 and 2*10^400, two different values, so the mapping has two different keys and the pointer `/2e400` finds the second (RFC 6901 section 4: a token matches a key by its text). YAML 1.2.2 section 10.2.1.4 says a float is an approximation whose range and accuracy depend on the implementation, and section 3.2.1.3 compares scalars by canonical form. Neither says whether two values that a double rounds alike are one key. The kit compares keys outside the range of a double by their exact decimal value (docs/edit-semantics.md, Refusals: 'Two float keys whose values lie outside the finite non-zero range of a binary64 double'), so that no valid document is refused because of the range of the library that reads it; that is a convention and the case carries the tag. A library may instead refuse the document with a `limit` error, as it may for integers beyond 64 bits; it must not call the keys duplicates. The case is a patch because the kit has no value for a float beyond the range of a double (a document would be read as infinity). The edit must change `b` only.

provenance.reference: A key identity that gave 1e400 and 2e400 the same identity, so a valid mapping was refused as a duplicate.
